description_full: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. develops, markets, and supports a range of products and services for IT security worldwide. It provides a multilevel security architecture that defends enterprises' cloud, network, mobile devices, endpoints information, and IOT solutions. The company offers Mesh Network Security, which comprises Firewall, Maestro Hyperscale Firewall, Firewall Software R82.10, Spark Firewall, and AI Powered Security Management for hybrid cloud, internet and perimeter gateways, and branch locations. It also provides Workspace Security Platform, including email, endpoint, mobile, browser, and XDR security solutions across devices, browsers, SaaS apps, and remote access. In addition, the company offers Threat Exposure Management platforms comprising threat intelligence, vulnerability detection and prioritization, and safe remediation. Further, it offers AI Security platforms comprising workforce and agent security, and red teaming solutions. Additionally, the company offers cyber security services, including managed detection and response, incident response, security consulting and managed, security consulting, professional, and training services. The company also provides technical customer support programs and plans; professional services in implementing, upgrading, and optimizing its products comprising design planning and security implementation; and certification and educational training services on its products. Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 6K people. Revenue per employee of $399K ranks in the above the sector median among Technology peers, with revenue growing 6%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $172K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $30K per employee reflects an ownership culture. financial_summary: Check Point Software Technologi is a large-cap technology business with a $15.0B market cap on $2.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 8% cost of capital — a 28-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 43 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.13× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 9.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 30% operating margin runs 24pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.30x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-15.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 32% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 10% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 26% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 41% and a beta of 0.62, it is more defensive than the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $139.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 31% in the 2020 crash, 27% in the 2022 bear market and 32% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 23% below its DCF fair value of $191, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 44%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $160 to $238 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 17.7 vs 27.4 and P/FCF 12.8 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 31% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.8% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 31 covering analysts target $153 on average, 4% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 36% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 28pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 3.24).
It converts 43% of revenue into free cash flow, or 35% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.13x.
ROE of 37% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.7x equity multiplier).
It spends 16.8% of revenue on R&D and 7.5% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $4.3B (12% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.4% over 3 years, 5.7% over 5 years and 5.3% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 0.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.08 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.0x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 9%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 1.0% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own 24.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 75%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (7 sales, net $9.2M sold).
It returns 9.3% a year to shareholders (9.3% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 5.1% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 6,825 employees, each generates about $399K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has grown 6.2% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $172K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $994K (2x revenue per employee).
